chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about one in Ihram who had intercourse with his wife, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He has come to a grievous matter.' I said, 'Issue a verdict to me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Did he coerce her or did he not coerce her?' I said, 'Issue a verdict regarding both together.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had coerced her, so upon him would be two sacrificial animals (badanatan); and if he did not happen to have coerced her, so upon him would be a sacrificial animal, and upon her would be a sacrificial animal, and they would both be separate from the place in which they did what they did, until they both end up to Makkah, and upon them both would be the Hajj of the next year, it being inevitable from it.'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So when they both end up to Makkah, so she would still be his wife just as she used to be?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. She would be his wife just as she used to be. So when they both end up to the place which from the two of them was what was, separated would be effected between them until they were free from their Ihram. So it would have been ended from them. My (peace be upon him) father (peace be upon him) was saying that'.

And in another report, '(He (peace be upon him) said): 'So if he was not able upon a sacrificial animal, so he should feed sixty poor ones, for each poor one being one Mudd. So if he was not able, then he should Fast for eighteen days, and upon her as well would be similar to it if he did not happen to have coerced her'.

key_terms.حَتَّى يُحِلَّا: Until they are free from Ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific measure of volume for food (approx. 750g)
key_terms.يَفْتَرِقَانِ: They separate (from the place of intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a husband and wife having intercourse during Hajj while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific expiation (kaffarah) for sexual intercourse during Hajj, distinguishing between coercion and voluntary acts by imposing double sacrifices on the coerced wife and single on the husband, or vice versa depending on the interpretation of 'badanah'. It further outlines the hierarchical compensation of feeding sixty poor persons or fasting eighteen days for those unable to afford animals, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on proportional justice. The ruling underscores the sanctity of the Ihram state, linking physical intimacy to ritual validity and requiring the couple to remain together until completing their respective expiations in Mecca.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about one in Ihraam falling upon his wife. So heasws said: ‘He has come to a grievous matter’. I said, ‘Issue a verdict to me’. So heasws said: ‘Did he coerce (force) her or did he not coerce her?’ I said, ‘Issue a verdict regarding both together’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he had coerced her, so upon him would be two sacrificial animals; and if did not happen to have coerced her, so upon him would be a sacrificial animal, and upon her would be a sacrificial animal, and they would both be separate from the place in which they did what they did, until they both end up to Makkah, and upon them both would be the Hajj of the next year, it being inevitable from it’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So when they both end up to Makkah, so she would still be his wife just as she used to be?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes. She would be his wife just as she used to be. So when they both end up to the place which from the two of them was what was, separated would be effected between them until they were free from their Ihraam. So it would have been ended from them. Myasws fatherasws was saying that’.

And in another report, ‘(Heasws said): ‘So if he was not able upon a sacrificial animal, so he should feed sixty poor ones, for each poor one being one Mudd (approximated 750 gms of food). So if he was not able, then he should Fast for eighteen days, and upon her as well would be similar to it if he did not happen to have coerced her’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram and is involved in sexual relation with his wife. He (the Imam) said, ‘He has done a great awfull thing.’ I said, ‘Grant us a Fatwa.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘I despise it, does he not despise it?’ I then said, ‘Grant us a Fatwa about both of them.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If she despised it, there are two badanah on him, if she did not despise, there is one badanah on him and she owes one badanah. They must stay away from each other from that place until they reach Makkah and they owe al-Hajj in future.’

I then said, ‘When they arrive in Makkah will she be his wife as before?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, she is his wife as before and when they arrive at the place where it had happened they still remain separated until they come out of the state of Ihram; it then ends. This is what my father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said.’”

In another Hadith it is said that if he cannot offer badanah he must feed sixty destitute people, one mud (a certain measurement) to each person, and if he cannot do this also he must fast eighteen days and the same rule applies to her case also.
